faq.question: Can I check my EPF balance without a UAN?
faq.answer: Not directly. The SMS, missed-call, website and app services all depend on your UAN. If you don't know it, it's printed on most salary slips, and HR can give it to you. Once you have it, activate it once on the member portal or in UMANG, and every method above will work.

faq.question: Why haven't I received the 2025–26 interest yet?
faq.answer: The 8.25% rate for 2025–26 was ratified on 19 June 2026, and EPFO credits it to members' accounts over the following months; reports suggested the process could run into September. If your passbook still shows no interest entry for 2025–26, check again after some weeks, and confirm your account had no pending transfers or KYC problems.

faq.question: Does the missed call service cost anything?
faq.answer: No. The call disconnects automatically after a couple of rings, so you aren't charged, and the SMS reply is free. It only works from the mobile number registered with your UAN.

faq.question: How do I download my old employer's EPF passbook?
faq.answer: Log in to the passbook site, choose Passbook and select the old employer's member ID from the list; you can view and download it like the current one. If the old ID doesn't appear, it isn't linked to your UAN yet, and you'll need to link it or transfer that balance through the member portal.

faq.question: Is the balance in the SMS the same as the passbook?
faq.answer: Both come from EPFO's records. The SMS gives a summary: the balance and the latest contribution. The passbook breaks it down by month, employer and employee shares, plus interest. If the figures look different, use the passbook to see exactly which entries make up the balance, and contact the EPFO helpline (1800118005) if something doesn't add up.
